lesson.subtitle: Lesson 8 -- Sorry, The Tenth?

lesson.grammar_point: echo questions and question tags for checking

listenings.text: Hi Fabia, this is David, very quickly, before my next call. We have forty-eight employees now, not forty-two. We want to be live on the first of March. Ralph signs the budget, and he is in London. I need the employee file from you by the tenth. The tenth, not the twentieth. If you cannot answer something today, write it down and send it by email.

Hi Fabia, this is Karen. Do not read the minutes yet, because they are wrong. There were six people on that call. David said the tenth. Then somebody said the twentieth, and nobody corrected it. So the minutes say the twentieth. A fourth person joined in the middle. He asked two questions, and he never said his name. Next time, please stop me and ask.

reading.source: Transcript of the recording you heard two slides ago.

gist.prompt: Reading it, what was the one thing he most wanted you to get right?
choices: That he is busy and the call has to be short.
The date of the file: the tenth, not the twentieth.
That Ralph is difficult to reach in London.

items: The old spreadsheet had the right number of employees.

The go-live date and the file date are the same day.

He corrects the date on purpose, in the same sentence.

Unanswered questions should be raised on the call itself.

matching.title: Match the word to its meaning
defs: to make something clear that was not clear
to say the same thing again, with different words
to hear and understand something as it goes past
to speak while another person is still speaking
to say the long thing again, short
the written record of what a meeting decided

items.situation: "We need it by the tenth." You are not sure it was the tenth.
tips: Sorry, the tenth or the twentieth?

items.situation: He said a name you have never heard. One question.
A whole sentence went past you. One line.
tips: Sorry, I didn't catch that last part.

items.situation: You heard it, but it made no sense. One line.
tips: I want to be sure I follow.

items.situation: Two people start speaking at the same time.
tips: Could we take these one at a time?

items.situation: The call is ending. Nobody said what happens next. One line.
tips: Before we close: you send the file, I send the proposal.
Before we close, just to confirm ...

casebank.label: Useful language
items: In A, I would have said ...
Seventy percent sure is not sure.
It cost a week, and one email would have ...
Nobody minds being asked a date twice.
In B, I would have asked who he was straight away.
It is harder to ask after ten minutes than after ten seconds.
C is the most expensive one, because ...
Silence sounds like agreement.
Interrupting costs five seconds. This cost ...
The summary at the end would have caught all three.
